entries.name: Amherst College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college with open curriculum; all students admitted to the college and declare majors (including Computer Science) later with no CS cap or separate selection at entry.

entries.name: Arizona State University
entries.basis: First-years apply directly to the CS BS (Fulton Schools), which uses published threshold criteria above ASU minimums (1210 SAT or 24 ACT or 3.00 ABOR GPA or top 25% rank, plus all HS math and science competencies complete), not a holistic cap. No CS-specific admit rate is published. Because the thresholds are only modestly above ASU's general criteria (overall rate 0.884), estimate ~0.80 (roughly 0.9x overall); applicants missing the bar are typically redirected to another ASU major.

entries.name: Auburn University
entries.basis: Auburn states that students accepted by the university are also accepted into the Samuel Ginn College of Engineering pre-engineering program (incl. pre-CS); no separate CS selection at entry. Students advance to the CS major later after completing pre-engineering requirements.

entries.name: Barnard College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college; students are admitted to Barnard as a whole and declare majors (including Computer Science, taught with Columbia) in sophomore year; no CS-specific selection at entry.

entries.name: Baylor University
entries.basis: Baylor admits first-years to the university with an intended major; CS (School of Engineering & Computer Science) has no separate first-year selection or published cap, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Binghamton University
entries.basis: CS is in the Watson College of Engineering and Applied Science, which runs its own first-year review and is described as more selective than Harpur/the university; no Watson or CS admit rate is published (checked Binghamton admissions, Pipe Dream, CDS-based aggregators). Structural estimate ~0.75x the 37.3% overall rate, consistent with engineering-school ratios at selective publics that admit by college.

entries.name: Boston College
entries.basis: CS (BA/BS) is in the Morrissey College of Arts & Sciences; BC admits to the undergraduate school with no CS-specific cap or separate selection, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Boston University
entries.basis: BU's CS department directs prospective majors to apply to the College of Arts & Sciences (the broad college); no CS-specific cap or published CS/CAS admit rate, so the CS rate is treated as the overall rate.

entries.name: Bowdoin College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college; all first-years admitted to the college and declare majors (incl. Computer Science) later, no CS-specific selection or cap at entry.

entries.name: Brandeis University
entries.basis: Single undergraduate college (College of Arts and Sciences); students admitted to the university and declare Computer Science later with no separate CS selection at entry.

entries.name: Brigham Young University
entries.basis: BYU catalog: BS Computer Science (and Software Engineering, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning emphases) is open enrollment; only the Animation emphasis is limited enrollment. Admission is to the university; no CS-specific selection at entry.

entries.name: Brown University
entries.basis: Open Curriculum; all undergraduates admitted to The College and declare concentrations (incl. Computer Science) by end of sophomore year. No separate CS or engineering admission at entry.

entries.name: California Institute of Technology
entries.basis: Caltech admits all first-years to the Institute with no major; students choose an option (incl. Computer Science) after the first year with no CS-specific selection at entry. CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: Carleton College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college: admits to the college as a whole; majors (incl. Computer Science) declared in sophomore year with no separate CS cap or selection at entry. CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: Carnegie Mellon University
entries.basis: First-years apply and are admitted directly to the School of Computer Science (SCS). CMU does not publish college-level admit rates (overall Fall 2025: 3,859/34,867 = 11.1%). Secondary sources converge on ~5% for SCS: College Transitions ('under five percent', flagged as non-institutional), Oriel Admissions ('under 5%'), Koppelman Group / Leland and others citing ~5-7%. Kept at ~5%.

entries.name: Case Western Reserve University
entries.basis: CWRU admits first-years to the university (single undergraduate admission); students may indicate interest but can declare or change into Computer Science (BS/BA) at any time with no CS-specific cap or selection at entry. CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: Chapman University
entries.basis: Applicants list an intended major and CS (Fowler School of Engineering) students are admitted through the single university-wide first-year review; Chapman publishes no separate CS/Fowler admit rate or cap (only Dodge film programs have separate selection).

entries.name: Claremont McKenna College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college; students admitted to the college and declare a major later (CS taken via the Claremont Colleges consortium). No separate CS selection.

entries.name: Clemson University
entries.basis: Clemson admits by first/second-choice major and lists Computer Science among majors with far more applicants than seats; CECAS is its most competitive college. No CS-specific count is published (statistics page gives only overall: Fall 2025 27,498/64,805 = 42%; Fall 2024 38%). Estimate = ~0.6x overall (~0.38), the CS-to-overall ratio seen at capped-major publics like Purdue and Virginia Tech.

entries.name: Colgate University
entries.basis: Liberal arts university; admission is to the university and the CS major is declared later. No separate CS selection.

entries.name: College of the Holy Cross
entries.basis: Liberal arts college with a single first-year admission; the CS major (Dept. of Mathematics and Computer Science) is declared after enrollment with no separate CS selection or cap at entry, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Columbia University in the City of New York
entries.basis: CS is offered in both Columbia College and Columbia Engineering (SEAS); applicants apply to one school through a single joint process and Columbia publishes only the combined CC+SEAS rate (no SEAS-only figure). CS is declared in sophomore year with no minimum requirements (CS dept FAQ), so there is no CS cap at entry and the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Cornell University
entries.basis: CS (Bowers CIS) can be entered via either the College of Engineering (B.S.) or the College of Arts and Sciences (B.A.), with identical CS requirements; students affiliate with the major after enrollment and there is no CS-specific cap at entry. Cornell's IRP publishes only university-wide admit totals (Fall 2025: 6,077/72,523 = 8.38%); no official Engineering or A&S rate is published, and third-party Engineering estimates conflict (about 9% vs about 23%), so the overall rate is used.

entries.name: Creighton University
entries.basis: CS (BS/BA) sits in the Department of Computer Science, Design & Journalism within the College of Arts and Sciences, the broad college most students enter; no CS-specific selection or cap at entry, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Dartmouth College
entries.basis: Dartmouth admits to the College as a whole; CS major is declared in sophomore year with no separate CS or engineering selection at entry. CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: Davidson College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college admitting to the college as a whole; CS major declared later with no CS cap. CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: Drexel University
entries.basis: Drexel admits first-years directly into a major (CS in the College of Computing & Informatics, Fall entry only; CCI undeclared also available). No published CS/CCI admit rate or CDS breakdown found. Estimate ~0.8x the overall rate (0.699) on the structural argument that high-demand majors (CS, engineering, nursing) are reported as tighter than the university overall, consistent with peers like Northeastern/RIT where direct-admit CS runs below the overall rate.

entries.name: Duke University
entries.basis: CS at Duke is a Trinity College of Arts & Sciences major declared by end of sophomore year; applicants choose Trinity vs Pratt (engineering) but CS has no cap or separate selection, so CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: Elon University
entries.basis: Elon admits first-years to the university as a whole; CS (Dept. of Computer Science, College of Arts & Sciences) has no separate selection or cap at entry, students may declare the major at any time. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: Emory University
entries.basis: CS is a major in Emory College of Arts and Sciences; first-years are admitted to Emory College (or Oxford College) with no CS-specific selection and declare a major by end of sophomore year. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: Fairfield University
entries.basis: Fairfield uses one holistic university admission; applicants indicate an intended school/major (CS is in the School of Engineering and Computing) but no separate CS/engineering admit rate or cap is published. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: Florida International University
entries.basis: FIU admits first-years to the university; the B.S. in Computer Science (Knight Foundation School of Computing and Information Sciences) is not a limited-access program at freshman entry, students can declare CS on admission. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: Florida State University
entries.basis: FSU CS department states undergraduate admission is handled by the university Office of Admissions; students may be admitted to the university without completing prerequisites but are not admitted to the CS major until they complete them. No separate CS selection at entry, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: George Washington University
entries.basis: CS is in the School of Engineering and Applied Science (SEAS); first-year applicants indicate their school/major on the common GW application and are admitted into SEAS with an intended major. GW publishes no SEAS- or CS-specific first-year admit rate and there is no evidence SEAS is more selective than the university, so the overall rate applies.

entries.name: Georgetown University
entries.basis: Computer Science is a major in Georgetown College of Arts & Sciences; applicants apply to the College (no CS-specific cap or separate CS selection) and declare the major later. The CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Georgia Institute of Technology
entries.basis: Georgia Tech College of Computing 2025 enrollment roundup: 1,547 first-year admits / 13,711 applications for CS and Computational Media combined = 0.1128 (Summer/Fall 2025 entry). Figure combines CS with CM; GT does not publish a CS-only rate.

entries.name: Georgia State University
entries.basis: CS (B.S.) is in the College of Arts & Sciences; first-years are admitted under the general university standards (USG Freshman Index / GPA minimums) and may declare CS at entry with no separate CS selection or cap.

entries.name: Gonzaga University
entries.basis: Gonzaga's School of Engineering & Applied Science has competitive direct admission for engineering majors, but its admission pages state that direct admission does not apply to computer science; CS applicants go through regular university first-year admission (no CS cap). Can't tell whether CS is declared at entry or later, so directAdmit is null.

entries.name: Grinnell College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college with an open curriculum; students are admitted to the college and declare a major (incl. CS) later. No separate CS selection at entry.

entries.name: Hamilton College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college with an open curriculum; students are admitted to the college and declare a concentration (incl. CS) later. No separate CS selection at entry.

entries.name: Harvard University
entries.basis: Harvard College admits to the College as a whole; Computer Science is a concentration declared later via my.harvard after a DUS-approved plan of study (SEAS CS advising). No separate SEAS/CS selection at entry, so the CS rate equals the overall rate.

entries.name: Harvey Mudd College
entries.basis: Harvey Mudd admits to the college; all students take the Common Core for three semesters and need not declare a major until the end of sophomore year. No separate CS selection at entry, so the CS rate equals the overall rate.

entries.name: Howard University
entries.basis: Howard admits first-years through a single university process (Common App, intended major chosen on application; B.S. Computer Science sits in the College of Engineering and Architecture). The CDS (2022-23) lists special program requirements only for art, music, dance, theatre and nursing; no engineering/CS-specific selection or published school-level admit rate found. Treated as the overall rate; moderate confidence.

entries.name: Indiana University Bloomington
entries.basis: No CS cap: Luddy direct admission is automatic for any IUB admit who declares a Luddy major by Nov 1 with a 3.75+ GPA and SAT 1310/ACT 28; others are admitted to IUB and can enter CS after ~12 credits with a 2.3-2.5 GPA (College Transitions rates switching 'less-to-moderate'). CS B.A. is also in the College of Arts and Sciences. Admission to CS is effectively the university's admission.

entries.name: Johns Hopkins University
entries.basis: JHU uses single-door admission (except Biomolecular Engineering): students are admitted to the university and declare CS in the Whiting School after enrolling; no CS cap at entry, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Kennesaw State University
entries.basis: KSU advising: the Computer Science program has no specific admission requirements; only admission to Kennesaw State is required to declare the major (progression requires B or better in CSE 1321/1322).

entries.name: Lehigh University
entries.basis: Lehigh admits first-years into a college (CS BS is in the P.C. Rossin College of Engineering; a BA in CS also exists in Arts & Sciences, plus the selective CSB program). Lehigh publishes only the overall rate (5,601/19,342 = 28.9%, Class of 2029), with no college-level rates; secondary sources (College Transitions, Empowerly) call engineering/CS more competitive but give no numbers. Estimate: Rossin slightly below overall (~0.85-0.9x), based on that structural argument.

entries.name: Marquette University
entries.basis: Marquette is direct-admit by college; CS sits in the broad Klingler College of Arts and Sciences, which has general college-prep requirements and no CS-specific cap. Marquette publishes no college-level admit rates (admitted student profile shows only GPA/test data), so the CS rate is treated as the overall rate.

entries.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
entries.basis: MIT admits all first-years to the Institute as a whole; stated field of interest does not affect admission, and students declare Course 6 (EECS) as early as spring of first year. No separate CS selection, so CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: Michigan State University
entries.basis: MSU admits first-years to the university in general (not to a college); CS requires a secondary College of Engineering admission after enrollment (28+ MSU credits, MTH 132/133, PHY 183, CSE 231, 3.0 combo GPA). No CS-specific selection at entry, so first-year CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: Middlebury College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college; applicants are admitted to the college and declare the CS major later (department's 'Navigating the Major' page describes declaration by enrolled students). No separate CS or engineering selection.

entries.name: New Jersey Institute of Technology
entries.basis: NJIT catalog lists uniform first-year admission requirements for all math/science/engineering/computing majors with no capped or competitive programs (only Honors College / accelerated programs differ). Students enter Ying Wu College of Computing majors without a separate CS selection, so CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: New York University
entries.basis: CS is offered both in the College of Arts and Science (Courant BA) and Tandon (BS). CAS students declare the CS major after CSCI-UA 101 with a C or better (cs.nyu.edu declaring page), with no CS cap. NYU does not publish school- or CS-level admit rates, so the CS rate is treated as the overall rate. College Transitions lists NYU as direct admit to CS with an easy change-in ('Less'). Tandon CS may be more selective, but no official number exists.

entries.name: North Carolina State University
entries.basis: All engineering first-years, CS included, are admitted to the College of Engineering's Engineering First Year program (engr.ncsu.edu), then compete to enter CS (College Transitions: 'competitive, not guaranteed'). NCSU publishes no Engineering admit count. COE annual report 2025-26: >13,000 applications and ~1,900 first-year enrollees for Fall 2026. At the university-wide yield (~31%: 6,090 enrolled / ~19,600 admitted of 47,900 at 41%), that implies ~6,100 admits (~47%). Engineering yield is probably higher, which would put the rate nearer 30-35%. Secondary sources disagree (~30% vs ~50%), so this is a labeled estimate of ~0.35 for the Engineering school.

entries.name: Northeastern University
entries.basis: Northeastern admits first-years directly into a college/major, and CS students go into Khoury College (College Transitions lists it as direct admit). It publishes no Khoury-specific admit rate. Overall rate for 2024-25: 5.2% (5,132 of 98,425, per College Transitions), and the regular-decision rate was ~3.8%. Khoury/CS is a high-demand college, so it is estimated below the overall rate at ~4%. Counselor sites claim 3-4%, but they are not independently sourced.

entries.name: Northwestern University
entries.basis: Applicants apply to one undergraduate school, but CS is offered both as a BA in Weinberg and a BS in McCormick, with no CS cap and no published school- or CS-level admit rate. College Transitions lists Northwestern as not direct-admit, with an easy change-in to CS ('Less'). The CS rate is treated as the overall rate.

entries.name: Ohio State University
entries.basis: Since Autumn 2023 the College of Engineering caps CSE/CIS as one of the 'Big 4' oversubscribed pre-majors: applicants must select the CSE (Pre) major on the Common App and are selected for it during university admission; students who enter other programs cannot transfer in later; pre-majors still apply to the full major after prerequisite coursework (COE memo, Jan 2023: 'hundreds more students desire CSE/CIS than the unit can teach'). No official CSE/COE first-year admit count is published (only unreliable SEO pages claim 20-30%). Estimate ~0.5x the overall 60.6% rate (Fall 2024), in line with capped public CS programs at Purdue and Virginia Tech.

entries.name: Pennsylvania State University
entries.basis: First-years are admitted to a campus and college (College of Engineering or Division of Undergraduate Studies), not the CS major; CS at University Park is under administrative enrollment controls, with entrance-to-major after 29-55 Penn State credits, required CMPSC/MATH/PHYS courses, and a minimum 3.20 GPA (Penn State Bulletin). Engineering admission to University Park is more competitive than the overall ~55% rate, but Penn State publishes no college-level admit rate; one low-quality aggregator (collegedunia) claims 24% for engineering, which is unverified. Estimate ~0.7x overall, by analogy with engineering-college selectivity at public peers that admit by college (e.g., Purdue, Virginia Tech).

entries.name: Pepperdine University
entries.basis: Pepperdine DOES offer CS bachelor's degrees through Seaver College: a BS in Computer Science/Mathematics and a BA in Computer Science/Philosophy (combined degrees, likely why no pure CS CIP row exists in our DB). Admission is to Seaver College through the standard undergraduate process; there is no separate CS admission or cap, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Pomona College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college: students are admitted to the college and declare majors later (students can switch into CS after arriving, per Pomona's own 'Why I Majored in Computer Science' story). No separate CS admission or major cap at entry, so the CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Princeton University
entries.basis: Princeton admissions: students apply to the University, not to departments/schools; A.B./B.S.E. choice on the application does not affect admission chances. CS (offered as both A.B. and B.S.E.) is declared after enrollment (B.S.E. spring of first year, A.B. spring of second year) with no CS cap at entry.

entries.name: Purdue University
entries.basis: Purdue Admissions 'Class Profile' page (Fall 2026) lists Computer Science as a competitive major with a 63.4% admit rate (overall 53.3%; College of Science 65%; Engineering 37.9%). Prior cycles per secondary sources: 35.9% (Class of 2028, the value currently in our DB) and 42.9% (Class of 2029).

entries.name: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
entries.basis: RPI admissions FAQ: students are admitted to the Institute; applicants pick an intended major (CS in School of Science) with flexibility to change; only Architecture/GSAS and the BS/MD program require direct application. No CS cap or CS-specific admit rate published (secondary '30-40%' CS figures are unsourced).

entries.name: Rice University
entries.basis: Rice does not admit by major or school: applicants list an intended major (plus two alternates) but majors are declared by end of sophomore year; Rice publishes no separate rate for the Brown School of Engineering (where CS sits) and has no CS cap at entry.

entries.name: Rochester Institute of Technology
entries.basis: RIT admits first-years into a specific program; the BS Computer Science (Golisano College) is direct-admit and internal transfer into it is competitive (College Transitions change-of-major table: direct admit Yes, 3.0 min GPA, 'Moderate-to-Very' difficulty). The CS department's own annual report says BS CS draws 2,750+ applications a year (>12% of all RIT undergrad applications), making it the highest-demand program, but RIT publishes no per-program admit counts. Estimate ~0.75x the 0.71 overall rate for an over-subscribed program; a commonly repeated '46.7% for CS' figure appears only on low-quality/spam pages and was not used.

entries.name: Rutgers University-New Brunswick
entries.basis: CS is in the School of Arts and Sciences (Rutgers' broad default school); there is no direct first-year admission to the CS major. Students declare after earning C or better in Calc I/II, Intro CS, Data Structures and Discrete Structures I, with no GPA cutoff or cap (cs.rutgers.edu 'Admission to the Major'). College Transitions also lists it as not direct-admit, 'Less-to-Moderate' difficulty. Note: the School of Engineering (which offers no CIP 11.0701 CS degree) is more selective, but CS students enter through SAS.

entries.name: Rutgers University-Newark
entries.basis: The BS Computer Science is offered by the Dept. of Mathematics and Computer Science in the School of Arts and Sciences-Newark, which is the campus's general admitting school. The 2022-25 Newark undergraduate catalog lists the CS major's course requirements with no admission-to-major GPA, cap or separate selection. So the CS rate equals the university's overall rate.

entries.name: Santa Clara University
entries.basis: SCU DOES offer a CS bachelor's: the Dept. of Mathematics and Computer Science in the College of Arts and Sciences grants a 'Bachelor of Science in Computer Science' (likely the CIP 11.0701 program; our DB's NO_CS_ROW looks wrong). The School of Engineering separately offers a BS in Computer Science and Engineering (likely CIP 14.0901). First-years apply to a school (Arts and Sciences, Business or Engineering) and may name a major; the CAS route to CS has no published cap or separate rate, so it is treated as the overall rate. Engineering and Business are described as more competitive, but SCU publishes no school-level admit rates (an '11% engineering' figure appears only on a low-quality site and was not used).

entries.name: Smith College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college admitting to the college as a whole; students declare majors (incl. Computer Science) between second semester of first year and sophomore spring with adviser approval only. No separate CS or engineering selection at entry.

entries.name: Southern Methodist University
entries.basis: First-years enter SMU as Lyle pre-majors and declare CS after completing subset courses (CSE 1341/1342, MATH 1337/1338, DISC, KNW 2300) with a minimum 2.5 subset GPA and C- or better; criteria-based, no cap or separate competitive selection at entry, so CS admission is SMU's overall admission.

entries.name: Stanford University
entries.basis: Stanford admits to the university; no separate School of Engineering or CS admission. Stanford Bulletin: declaring the CS major has no prerequisite course or major requirements; students declare by end of sophomore year.

entries.name: Stevens Institute of Technology
entries.basis: Stevens admits first-years by program; its undecided-pathway page says prospective CS/cybersecurity students must apply directly to that program (CS sits in the new School of Computing, not open to undecided students). No CS-specific admit counts published (fact sheets/CDS give only overall ~0.43-0.51). Estimate ~0.8x the 0.507 overall rate, reflecting CS being among the top-3 majors and a direct-admit program, by analogy to private tech peers with major-based admission (RPI, WPI) where CS runs somewhat below overall.

entries.name: Stony Brook University
entries.basis: Undergraduate Bulletin: all CEAS programs limit enrollment; qualified freshmen who indicate CS may be admitted directly as degree majors, others enter as pre-majors (AOI) and must apply later. No CS-level admit counts published. Estimate ~0.6x the 48% overall rate, the typical ratio for capped CS at publics with direct-major admission (e.g. Purdue, UMass Amherst, Rutgers).

entries.name: Swarthmore College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college admitting to the college as a whole; students declare majors (incl. CS) in sophomore year, no CS cap or separate engineering/CS selection at entry. CS rate equals the overall rate.

entries.name: Syracuse University
entries.basis: First-years apply to a specific college; CS majors are admitted directly into the College of Engineering and Computer Science. Syracuse does not publish a CDS or college-level admit rates. Low-quality secondary sites cite STEM programs near 45% vs 48.8% overall (Fall 2025: 22,756 / 46,645); estimate set slightly below overall since ECS is not known to be far more selective than the university.

entries.name: Temple University
entries.basis: CS is in the College of Science and Technology; first-years are admitted through the general university process with their chosen major, with no CS-specific cap or separate selection found (only Fox/Honors are noted as tighter). Students missing math prerequisites start undeclared in CST. CS rate equals the overall rate.

entries.name: Texas Christian University
entries.basis: TCU's CS program page states there are no special admission requirements for the computer science program; students are admitted through TCU's general holistic review and may list CS as their major (BS, College of Science & Engineering). No CS cap or separate selection found.

entries.name: Tufts University
entries.basis: Applicants choose School of Arts & Sciences or School of Engineering, but CS is offered in both (BA in A&S, BS in Engineering) and majors are declared later. Tufts does not publish school-level rates for recent cycles; historical Tufts figures showed Engineering admitting at or slightly above the A&S rate (e.g. Class of 2017: A&S 18.5%, Engineering 19.7%), so no CS/engineering selectivity premium. Class of 2029 overall 10.5% (Tufts Daily).

entries.name: Tulane University
entries.basis: All first-years are admitted to Tulane (Newcomb-Tulane College); CS majors declare later by submitting a major declaration form to the CS department in the School of Science & Engineering. No CS cap or separate CS/engineering selection at entry.

entries.name: University at Buffalo
entries.basis: First-years select CS as an intended major and are reviewed holistically by the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences with UB Admissions (no separate application); they must then complete core courses (CSE 115/116, Calc 1, Discrete; core GPA >= 2.5, overall GPA >= 2.8) to be accepted into the major. UB publishes no CS or SEAS first-year admit rate and none was found in CDS or College Transitions. Estimate is structural: ~0.8x the 80.6% overall rate, reflecting SEAS's stronger applicant pool and secondary sources calling CS capacity-limited; low confidence.

entries.name: University of California-Davis
entries.basis: UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Computer Science broad discipline (all CIP 11), UC Davis Fall 2025: 946 admits / 4,893 applicants = 19.3% (shows 19%) vs 44% campus overall. Fall 2023 was also 19% (989/5,256) per UC Newsroom. Engineering discipline 39% (6,935/17,866). CS admits are selected by major (CS in L&S and CSE in Engineering).

entries.name: University of California, Berkeley
entries.basis: Rated route: Computer Science major in the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS), where first-years apply to and are admitted directly into the CS major (cdss.berkeley.edu/admissions). UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Berkeley, broad discipline Computer Science (CDSS), Fall 2025: 629 admits / 9,750 applicants = 6.45% (vs 11% campus). Alternative EECS route is not reported separately; it sits in Engineering (College of Engineering etc.): 1,788 / 25,025 = 7.1%.

entries.name: University of California, Irvine
entries.basis: UCI admits by major (CS in the Bren School of ICS; applicants admitted to primary or alternate major). UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Irvine, broad discipline Computer Science, Fall 2025: 1,874 admits / 6,794 applicants = 27.6% (campus overall 29%). Broad discipline may include other ICS computing majors besides CS proper.

entries.name: University of California, Los Angeles
entries.basis: UCLA First-Year Profile by major, Fall 2025: Computer Science (Samueli School of Engineering, direct admit to major) 6,806 applicants, 7.3% admit rate. Related: Computer Science and Engineering 7.2% (2,446 applicants), Computer Engineering 4.7%. Cross-check: UC Information Center discipline dashboard, UCLA Computer Science, 498 / 6,803 = 7.3%.

entries.name: University of California, Riverside
entries.basis: UC campuses admit first-years to a major; CS at UCR is in the Bourns College of Engineering. UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Riverside, broad discipline Computer Science, Fall 2025: 4,111 admits / 5,068 applicants = 81.1% (campus overall 87%). Only mildly more selective than the campus; direct-admit status inferred from UC admit-by-major practice, not separately confirmed (search budget exhausted).

entries.name: University of California, San Diego
entries.basis: UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Computer Science broad discipline (CIP family 11), UCSD Fall 2025: 2,143 admits / 10,785 applicants = 19.9% (dashboard shows 20%) vs 28% campus overall. Engineering discipline at UCSD was 19% (3,938/20,205). CS is a selective major admitted by applied major.

entries.name: University of California, Santa Barbara
entries.basis: UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Computer Science broad discipline (all CIP 11), UCSB Fall 2025: 1,989 admits / 5,865 applicants = 33.9% (shows 34%) vs 38% campus overall; Engineering discipline 21% (2,694/12,679). CS is in the College of Engineering, which selects freshmen by major. DOUBT: 34% looks high for UCSB CS (older reports ~5-18% for CoE/CS); CIP-11 bucket may include non-CoE computing programs. Engineering 21% is a plausible alternative.

entries.name: University of California, Santa Cruz
entries.basis: UC Information Center 'Freshman admission by discipline' dashboard, Computer Science broad discipline (all CIP 11), UCSC Fall 2025: 4,725 admits / 5,952 applicants = 79.4% (shows 79%) vs 72% campus overall; Engineering 77% (3,961/5,134). DOUBT: CS rate above campus rate despite UCSC treating CS as a capped/selective major (College Transitions flagged the same anomaly); unit MAJOR is based on that reputation, not confirmed on a UCSC page (search budget ran out).

entries.name: University of Chicago
entries.basis: UChicago CS department states undergraduate admission is handled by the University (single College admission, no separate CS track); students declare the CS major after enrolling with no prerequisites/GPA gate (College Transitions 'Changing to CS' table). CS rate equals overall rate.

entries.name: University of Colorado Boulder
entries.basis: CU Boulder IR public Tableau report #1017 (First-Year Admissions Counts), Summer/Fall first-year, Major = 'CSEN - Computer Science' (BS, College of Engineering & Applied Science): Fall 2026 873 admitted / 1,189 applied = 0.734. Fall 2025 was 1,226 / 1,881 = 0.652. Including the CS BA (CSEN - Computer Science (BA)) Fall 2026: 1,021 / 1,444 = 0.707. Overall Fall 2026 = 54,024 / 71,197 = 0.759, so CS is only modestly more selective. First-years apply to a major and are admitted by college (CEAS); IUT available later.

entries.name: University of Connecticut
entries.basis: No published CS admit rate found. UConn's Nov 2024 Senate report (First-Year Applicants, Admits & Enrollees by Major) says applicants apply to a first-choice major; programs with 'true space constraints' (CS in the College of Engineering is the top-growth applicant program, +1,539 apps Fall 2021->2024) send competitive applicants to a second-choice major or ACES. Report shows only deltas, not rates. Structural estimate: space-capped CS ~0.75x the ~0.54 overall rate -> ~0.40. Low confidence.

entries.name: University of Delaware
entries.basis: No CS- or college-level admit counts published (UD IRE dashboards/CDS give only university-wide figures; overall Fall 2024 ~27,517/39,742 = 0.69). Freshmen are admitted by central admissions directly into the CISC major (College of Engineering); College Transitions rates internal transfer into UD engineering 'Moderate/Very' difficult, implying a capped, more selective major. Structural estimate: engineering/CS ~0.8x overall -> ~0.55. Low confidence.

entries.name: University of Florida
entries.basis: UF CISE: freshman applicants do not apply to the department but to the University of Florida in general, and declare the major (CS/CSE) at UF Preview; no CS-specific selection at entry (separate department applications apply only to transfers/change of major). CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: University of Georgia
entries.basis: UGA CS dept: first-years select 'Intended Computer Science' on the UGA application; admission to UGA does not admit to the CS major. Students apply to the major later after meeting entrance requirements (C or better in CSCI 1302/2610/2720 within two attempts, 2.7 GPA across them, plus CSCI 1301 and MATH 2250; rules for Fall 2025+ matriculants). No CS selection at entry, so entry rate = overall UGA rate.

entries.name: University of Illinois Chicago
entries.basis: CS is in UIC's College of Engineering; UIC says each college has its own criteria for selecting applicants, and Engineering admits have a clearly higher profile (middle-50% GPA 3.6-4.0, SAT 1310-1470) than LAS (3.4-3.9, 1240-1430) or Business (3.3-3.8, 1210-1380). Students who transfer in later need a 3.00 GPA plus Calc I and CS 111. No published Engineering or CS admit counts found (CDS has no breakdown by college; search budget ran out before a deeper check). Structural estimate: at peer UIUC, the engineering college admits about 0.6x the overall rate (Grainger 21.2% vs 36.6% overall, Fall 2025), and 0.6-0.7x UIC's 75.8% overall gives about 0.45-0.53, so ~0.50.

entries.name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
entries.basis: UIUC Undergraduate Admissions published first-choice admit rates, Fall 2025 cycle: Computer Science (Grainger) 7.4%, CS+X 17.4%, Grainger 21.2%, total 36.6%. This replaces the earlier 7.2% (Fall 2024 version of the same page: CS 7.2%, CS+X 18.1%, Grainger 24.2%, total 42.4%). The current page (2026 first-year cycle, admissions.illinois.edu/admit-rates/) shows only college-level rates (Grainger 23.3%, total 38.1%, first-choice 32.8%) and no CS-specific rate, so Fall 2025 is the newest CS figure. Fall 2025 values come from the archived official page (Wayback snapshots 2025-11-26 and 2026-05-04), also confirmed by College Transitions.

entries.name: University of Iowa
entries.basis: The CS major (BA/BS) is in the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences; UI Admissions' CS page says students only need to meet the requirements for admission to CLAS, with no separate CS selection or cap. (The separate Computer Science and Engineering degree in the College of Engineering uses guaranteed RAI-based direct admission, not a competitive cap.)

entries.name: University of Maryland
entries.basis: CS is a Limited Enrollment Program and first-years are admitted directly to the major, with about 600 seats for enrolled freshmen from Fall 2024 (up from 450) and transfers cut to about 100 (UMD CS 'First Year Applicants' and the CS LEP FAQ; Diamondback 12/6/2023). UMD publishes no CS applicant or admit counts. IRPA's Fall 2025 summary has only campus figures: 30,282 admitted / 67,178 applicants = 45.1%, with 21.6% yield. Estimate: an April 2024 open-house speaker said about 9,000 applicants listed CS (reported only on a DCUrbanMom forum; ~10,000 for Fall 2025 after 12% application growth). 600 enrolled at an assumed 30-40% yield means ~1,500-2,000 admits, so ~15% (plausible range 10-20%). The forum's '600 admitted out of 9,000' (6.7%) seems to mix up the 600 enrolled seats with admits. Secondary sites quoting 26-30% are unsourced and come from before the 2024 change.

entries.name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
entries.basis: UMass UAIR Fall 2025 Admissions & Enrollment Report, Table ADM-1: Manning College of Information and Computer Sciences first-year applicants 4,991, accepted to 1st-choice major 2,362 -> 2,362 / 4,991 = 47.3% (vs 59% campus). First-years apply directly to the CS major (CICS 'Joining the Major' page). Rate is CICS-wide (CS plus Informatics), CS is the large majority; the 50.7% figure also counts admits to an alternate major.

entries.name: University of Miami
entries.basis: CS is a department in the College of Arts and Sciences (csc.as.miami.edu), the university's largest school (39% of the entering class). Applicants choose a school/major on the application, but UM publishes no school- or major-level admit rates and no CS cap; its class profile gives only the overall rate (22%, 11,961 / 54,218, Fall 2026 profile). Treat the CS rate as the university rate.

entries.name: University of Michigan
entries.basis: CSE admissions page: the Fall 2023+ CS advance-selection cap was removed as of Spring 2026; CS is now open to any College of Engineering or LSA student who meets declaration requirements, so CS entry is the university admission (declared later). Note: CoE itself admits separately from LSA, but CS-LSA path makes the university rate the relevant one.

entries.name: University of Minnesota-Twin Cities
entries.basis: First-years are admitted to a college (B.S. CS via College of Science and Engineering, B.A. via CLA), then apply to the CS major after prerequisites (usually sophomore year). UMN does not publish CSE applicant/admit counts; CSE's admitted middle-50% (GPA 3.62-4.00, ACT 29-34, Fall 2025) is the highest of all freshman colleges vs ~0.79 overall. Estimate ~0.55 assumes CSE admits roughly 0.7x the overall rate, in line with selective-engineering-college gaps at high-admit flagships; an unverified secondary snippet cited ~50% for CSE.

entries.name: University of Missouri
entries.basis: MU catalog: CS is in the College of Engineering, and students pursuing BS degrees in the College of Engineering must meet MU's General Admission Standard (plus recommended HS math/science coursework); no separate CS cap or selection found, so CS admission is the university admission.

entries.name: University of New Hampshire
entries.basis: UNH admissions decisions page lists competitive majors as many health/human-services programs and all business majors; CS (CEPS) is not among them. First-years apply to a major (CEPS also offers a 'Steps to CEPS' pathway for those not admitted directly), so CS admission is effectively the university admission.

entries.name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
entries.basis: First-years are admitted to UNC as a whole; there is no CS-specific selection at entry. The CS major's cap is applied after enrollment: students apply internally once enrolled in/after COMP 210 (competitive since 2022-23, ~300 seats/yr per department). The catalog confirms admission occurs after introductory coursework. For the Fall 2026 internal cycle the department says it expects to accept all eligible applicants subject to grade requirements. No first-year CS admit numbers are published.

entries.name: University of Notre Dame
entries.basis: Notre Dame admits to the university. Applicants give a non-binding college/major intent; a CS intent is not separately selected or capped at entry (only Business has a capacity policy). Engineering does not publish a separate admit rate (Koppelman Group, 2026). Students in the College of Engineering's first-year program declare CS after the first year.

entries.name: University of Pennsylvania
entries.basis: Penn admits applicants to one of four undergraduate schools; BSE Computer Science is in SEAS, and admitted SEAS students can declare CIS directly. Penn does not publish school-level admit rates. A secondary source reports SEAS admitted ~7.3% for the Class of 2024, when Penn overall was ~8%, so SEAS runs ~0.9x overall. Applied to the Class of 2029 overall rate of 4.9% (3,530/72,544), that gives ~4.5%. This rests on a single, weak secondary source; treat it as an estimate. CS is also available as a BA in the College (overall-rate admission).

entries.name: University of Pittsburgh-Pittsburgh Campus
entries.basis: Pitt first-years apply to a specific first-year entry school (admissions.pitt.edu). The School of Computing and Information (home of CS) has admitted first-years directly since 2019-20. No SCI applicant/admit counts were found (Pitt IR fact book has no breakdown by school). The estimate reasons from structure: Fall 2025 SCI admits had a 1310-1450 SAT middle 50%, modestly above Pitt overall. At other publics with school-level CS entry, the computing school admits at roughly 0.7-0.8x the overall rate. 0.75 x 0.5945 = ~0.45. Labeled estimate.

entries.name: University of Richmond
entries.basis: Richmond admits to the university and all first-years matriculate into the School of Arts & Sciences; no separate application to any school, program or major; CS declared in sophomore year. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: University of Rochester
entries.basis: Applicants apply to the University as a whole, not to a major or to the Hajim School; CS (in Hajim) is declared in sophomore year after CSC 171/172 and MATH 150 with GPA >= 2.0. No CS cap at entry. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: University of San Diego
entries.basis: USD Shiley-Marcos School of Engineering states all students are admitted as undeclared and there are no impacted majors; CS chosen after admission. CS rate = overall rate.

entries.name: University of South Florida
entries.basis: FTIC students who meet USF admission criteria are admitted into a Bellini College (AI, Cybersecurity & Computing) program; CS was historically a limited-access engineering program, but its first-year threshold (SAT Math >= 610 or ACT Math >= 26 or USF GPA 3.6, per 2020-21 CoE overview) sits below the typical USF admit profile (admit mid-range SAT ~1290-1420), so there is no meaningful separate CS selection. CS rate treated as overall rate; mild doubt since program-specific requirements may still apply.

entries.name: University of Southern California
entries.basis: USC does not publish a Viterbi or CS first-year admit rate (Koppelman Group: 'USC doesn't release a separate acceptance rate from Viterbi'; consultant sites only say CS is below the overall rate). Applicants are admitted into their first-choice major, reviewed with Viterbi. Estimate ~0.65x the overall rate (~10-11%), in line with direct-admit CS at peers such as UT Austin and UW Allen School that run well below their overall rates. Not sourced from counts.

entries.name: University of Tennessee
entries.basis: CS is in the Tickle College of Engineering, which admits first-years separately using a threshold (SPI = ACT math + 10x core GPA >= 60 and ACT math >= 25 / SAT math >= 590, with holistic review below that; class 'may be limited by space'). Applicants who miss it are admitted as University Exploratory and may transfer in later. No published engineering/CS admit rate found. Estimate ~0.8x the overall rate (0.38), reflecting a moderate threshold rather than a hard cap.

entries.name: University of Texas at Austin
entries.basis: UT Austin admits by major; CS (College of Natural Sciences) is a capped direct-admit major and top-%-auto-admits are not guaranteed CS. UT does not publish CS admit counts (Tex Admissions, a former UT admissions officer: 'UT refuses to make the CS admissions statistics public'; last official figure was Office of Admissions Dec 2016, >20% on ~2,700 apps). College Transitions publishes only McCombs counts. Secondary sources disagree: Tex Admissions <10% (Fall 2022 projection, ~10,000 apps / ~600 spots) and possibly <4% recently (~700 admits / 10-13k apps); instateutaustin.com 5-8%; appybara 10-15%. Spread too wide for CONSENSUS, so downgraded from 0.085 CONSENSUS to an 0.08 ESTIMATE (midpoint of the clustered 5-10% sources).

entries.name: University of Virginia
entries.basis: First-years apply to a specific school in separate pools; the BS in CS is in the School of Engineering and Applied Science (first-year target ~725), which College Transitions describes as generally more selective than the College (CS BA is also offered via the College, declared later). UVA does not publish school-level first-year admit rates in sources reachable here (IRA admissions page blocked; Class Profile PDF not text-readable). Estimate ~0.9x the Fall 2025 overall rate of 15.6% (64,457 apps / 10,086 admits). Catalog overall 0.23 looks like an older cycle.

entries.name: University of Washington-Seattle Campus
entries.basis: Allen School Direct-to-Major (CS/CE) published stats, 2026 cycle: WA 493/1,205 (41%), domestic non-resident 243/2,995 (8%), international 37/1,049 (4%); total 773 admits / 5,249 applicants = 0.1473. Prior cycle (2025): 810/6,946 = 0.1166. Figures cover CS and CE combined; residents far more likely to be admitted.

entries.name: University of Wisconsin-Madison
entries.basis: CS is in the College of Letters & Science with no capped entry; students declare after earning credit for COMP SCI 300 and MATH 222, BC or higher in an intro CS course, and a 2.25 GPA. Declaration is not competitive, so the CS rate is the university admit rate.

entries.name: Vanderbilt University
entries.basis: Applicants choose an undergraduate school (CS is offered in both the School of Engineering and the College of Arts & Science), but Vanderbilt does not admit to specific majors in those schools and publishes no school-level admit rate; admissions says no school is easier to get into. CS rate is taken to equal the overall rate.

entries.name: Vassar College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college with no CS-specific selection at entry; students declare the CS major later by form once they meet department requirements (department FAQ).

entries.name: Villanova University
entries.basis: Villanova's BS in Computer Science is housed in the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (Department of Computing Sciences), not the College of Engineering; no CS cap or separate CS selection found. Villanova's official admission profile publishes only university-wide figures (Class of 2030: 28,867 applicants, 29.6% admitted), no college-level rates. Third-party claims that CS is in Engineering at ~16-19% (orieladmissions) are wrong about where CS sits and are unsourced.

entries.name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
entries.basis: First-years who want CS are admitted to the College of Engineering's General Engineering program and move into CS after their first year (eng.vt.edu: CS applicants 'will begin their academic journey in the general engineering program'; only Building Construction admits directly). VT's University DataCommons admissions dataset (Office of Analytics & AI), Fall first-year applicants, College of Engineering: Fall 2026 (AY 2026-27) 16,055 offers / 22,972 applicants = 0.6989 (university 37,204 / 58,108 = 0.6403); Fall 2025 (AY 2025-26) 13,066 / 23,186 = 0.5635 (university 31,515 / 57,755 = 0.5457, matching our DB overall); Fall 2024 11,591 / 21,310 = 0.5439. Almost all of it is the General Engineering code (GE, CIP 99.0005). There is no CS-specific first-year selection in the data, so Engineering is about 1.03-1.09x the overall rate. The real CS filter is the competitive change-of-major after first year, which this rate does not capture.

entries.name: Wake Forest University
entries.basis: Wake Forest has one undergraduate admission and CS students apply through the university. Students declare the CS major later, after completing CSC 111/112 (the CS department says at least 40 credit hours) with a 2.0 GPA in CSC courses. The bulletin mentions no enrollment cap. The CS rate is the overall rate.

entries.name: Washington and Lee University
entries.basis: Liberal-arts university; CS is a department major in a liberal arts setting starting from an intro Python sequence, with no separate CS admission or cap found on the department page. Students are admitted to W&L and declare later. (Web search budget was exhausted; classified from official department page only.)

entries.name: Washington University in St. Louis
entries.basis: WashU says 'Applicants must apply to a specific school', and the CS degrees are in the McKelvey School of Engineering, so CS-intended students apply to McKelvey. WashU publishes no school-level admit rates (not in its CDS, admissions pages or College Transitions). This is an estimate: about 0.85x the overall 11.9% (CDS), because McKelvey's applicant pool is CS-heavy and secondary guides describe engineering as among WashU's most competitive entry points. That ratio follows the usual pattern at private universities that admit by school, where engineering/CS runs about 0.8-1.0x overall. Low confidence.

entries.name: Wellesley College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college; CS major and minor offered by a department, with no separate admission, cap or school-level selection found on the official CS page. Students are admitted to the college and declare later. (Web search budget was exhausted; classified from official department page only.)

entries.name: Wesleyan University
entries.basis: Liberal-arts university; CS major offered by the Mathematics & Computer Science department, with no separate admission or cap found on the official department page. Students are admitted to Wesleyan and declare later. (Web search budget was exhausted; classified from official department page only.)

entries.name: William & Mary
entries.basis: CS now sits in W&M's School of Computing, Data Sciences & Physics (cdsp.wm.edu). Neither the school/department pages nor the undergraduate admission page showed any separate first-year application, cap or selection for CS. First-years are admitted to W&M and declare a major later. (Web search budget was exhausted; this could not be fully confirmed, so it is worth rechecking later.)

entries.name: Williams College
entries.basis: Liberal arts college with a single undergraduate admission and no engineering school; the 2026-27 catalog describes CS as an ordinary department major open to all students, with no separate selection or cap at entry. Majors are declared after enrollment.

entries.name: Worcester Polytechnic Institute
entries.basis: WPI admits first-years to the institute as a whole. Its CS BS page says undecided applicants are welcome to apply and explore before committing, and the catalog's major-designation policy ties the major to completing the distribution requirements and the MQP. No CS cap or separate CS selection was found. directAdmit is null because applicants can list an intended major but there is no confirmed direct admission into a capped CS program.

entries.name: Yale University
entries.basis: Yale admissions FAQ: all undergraduates enroll in one college (Yale College) with access to the same programs and majors. There is no separate admission to engineering or CS, and majors are chosen after enrolling.
